title: Sunk Cost Trap
equation: Continue If: Expected Future Value > Future Cost (ignoring sunk cost)
hook: I've already put so much into this. That's the worst reason there is to keep going.
statement: What you already spent shouldn't drive your next decision. Only what's ahead of you should.
explainer: Founders keep pouring money into dying projects because quitting feels like admitting a mistake. That money's gone either way. Set kill criteria in advance and reward people for stopping bad bets.
sop: Figure out the future cost to keep going.
Compare the two without mentioning what you've spent.
If value is lower than cost, kill it or pivot.
Move the freed-up time and money to better work.
equation_example: You've spent $80,000. Finishing costs $20,000 more. Expected Future Value is $35,000. $35,000 beats $20,000, so keep going, and ignore the $80,000. If Future Cost were higher than future value, you'd stop, no matter what's already spent.
question: Pick one project and answer this honestly: if I hadn't started it, would I start it today?
closing_statement: What you already spent has no vote in this.
caption:
Principle Nº 297: Sunk Cost Trap

I've already put so much into this. That's the worst reason there is to keep going.

What you already spent shouldn't drive your next decision. Only what's ahead of you should.

Your turn: Pick one project and answer this honestly: if I hadn't started it, would I start it today?
